samples.summary: Header/footer selection highlight ignores `lineAffinity`, so it now disagrees with the caret after this change
samples.evidence: `getHFPositionFromMouse` (text-editor.ts:4437) and `resolveHFCellOffset` (text-editor.ts:4550) now return `'forward'` for a hit that lands on a wrap boundary, and that affinity is stored on the selection endpoints (`updateDragSelection`, text-editor.ts:1792-1798). The consumer that paints the HF highlight, `computeHFSelectionRects` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:798) and its helpers `hfFlatLayoutRects` (editor.ts:709-764) and `computeHFTableCellSelectionRects` (editor.ts:566), never read `lineAffinity` — the flat scan at editor.ts:864-873 uses only `anchor.offset` / `focus.offset`. The HF caret resolver (`computeHFCursorPixel`, editor.ts:508-515, and `computeHFTableCellCaretPixel`, editor.ts:419-426) *does* honour it, so an HF drag ending on a soft-wrap boundary now draws the caret at the start of the next line while the highlight still ends on the previous line. Before this change every HF hit-test returned `'backward'`, so the two agreed.
searchedFor: read editor.ts:377-535 (HF caret resolvers, which DO handle affinity)

samples.summary: Rewritten `getWrapAffinity` can now throw where it previously returned 'backward' (doc.getBlock on a stale layout)
samples.evidence: The old `getWrapAffinity` only did `layout.blocks.find(...)` and could not throw. It now delegates to `getVisualLineRange`, whose cell branch calls `this.doc.getBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` (text-editor.ts:4062) and `this.doc.getBlock(pos.blockId)` (text-editor.ts:4085); `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:187), and the branch also dereferences `tableBlock.tableData!.rows[...]` unchecked. `cellInfo` comes from the cached layout's `blockParentMap` (`getCellInfo`, text-editor.ts:3134-3139), so if the layout is momentarily stale relative to the model — e.g. `setCompositionStartPosition` (text-editor.ts:333) which is documented as running *after a remote change*, or the paste paths at text-editor.ts:3646/3701/3773 — an entry that names a table the model no longer has turns a formerly harmless 'backward' into an uncaught exception on the typing/IME/paste path. Fix belongs on the new `getWrapAffinity`/`getVisualLineRange` (use the non-throwing `doc.findBlock`, or guard). To confirm: whether any caller can reach `getWrapAffinity` while `blockParentMap` names a block absent from the model.

samples.summary: Nested-table cells: the click path now yields 'forward' but the typing path (`getWrapAffinity`) still cannot, so they disagree
samples.evidence: `resolveOffsetInNestedTable` now returns `hitTestLineAffinity(...)` (text-editor.ts:5008-5022), so a click on a wrap boundary inside a *nested* table cell produces 'forward'. But `getVisualLineRange`'s cell branch resolves the owning table with `layout.blocks.find(b => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId)` (text-editor.ts:4058), which only matches top-level layout blocks — a nested table block is not one, so it falls through to the `!lb` case (text-editor.ts:4091-4092) and returns [0,0]. `getWrapAffinity` therefore still answers 'backward' for nested-cell blocks, so typing one character after such a click silently resets the affinity and End stops moving again — exactly the symptom the change is meant to fix, left in place for nested tables.

samples.summary: Cell selection anchors now carry 'forward'; on a backwards drag that anchor becomes `end` in buildRects and can over-extend the highlight by a line
samples.evidence: `buildRects` reads `endAffinity = end.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:261) and `getNormalizedRange` returns endpoints as stored, only reordering them (selection.ts:703-713). The diff makes a single click inside a cell store 'forward' on *both* range endpoints (text-editor.ts:1603-1613), so a subsequent backwards drag/shift-click makes a 'forward' anchor the range `end`, and the cell branch (selection.ts:268-269 via resolvePositionPixel) then resolves that end to the start of the following visual line, painting one line more than is selected. Same class of issue already exists for body clicks (text-editor.ts:1532-1536), which is why confidence is low, but cell anchors are newly affected.

samples.summary: Two callers of the changed `CellHitTest` contract still drop the new `lineAffinity` field
samples.evidence: `resolveOffsetInCell` now returns `CellHitTest` including `lineAffinity`, and the shift-click / single-click callers were updated (text-editor.ts:1589-1595, 1603-1613). The triple-click caller (text-editor.ts:1564-1570) and the double-click caller (text-editor.ts:1573-1580) still build `DocPosition`s without it and call `this.cursor.moveTo(end)` / `moveTo(focus)` with no affinity argument, so `Cursor.moveTo` defaults to 'backward' (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28). When a word/block boundary in a cell coincides with a soft-wrap boundary the caret is drawn on the line above the selected word, and a following End keypress does nothing — the inconsistency the rest of the change removes.

samples.summary: `onCursorMove` dedupe key is a JSON.stringify of `cursor.position`, so the newly added `lineAffinity` property changes the key
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:614 builds `JSON.stringify({ cur: cursor.position, sel: selRange })` as the dedupe key for the cursor-move callback. Positions produced by the newly affinity-carrying hit-test paths add an own `lineAffinity` property, so a hit that only changes affinity (same blockId/offset) now produces a different key and fires an extra `cursorMoveCallback`. Harmless (a toolbar refresh), but it is an out-of-diff consumer that treats DocPosition as a value object.

verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim: getWrapAffinity (text-editor.ts:4140-4143) now routes through getVisualLineRange, whose cell branch calls the throwing Doc.getBlock at text-editor.ts:4062 and 4085 and dereferences tableData!.rows[rowIndex].cells[colIndex] unchecked at 4063; Doc.getBlock throws at document.ts:187 (non-throwing findBlock exists at document.ts:193). cellInfo comes from the cached layout via getCellInfo (text-editor.ts:3134-3139), and that cache is genuinely stale relative to the model on a reachable path: editor.ts:2126 passes `() => layout`, invalidateLayout (editor.ts:1407-1410) only drops layoutCache while `layout` is replaced only during recomputeLayout/render (editor.ts:1255-1299), and the remote-change handler at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:365-381 calls getDoc().refresh() and then updateCompositionStartPosition (line 373 -> editor.ts:3622 -> text-editor.ts:333 -> getWrapAffinity) BEFORE editor.render() at line 380. A remote deletion of the table (or of a row/column) therefore leaves blockParentMap naming a block/row the refreshed model lacks, turning a formerly harmless 'backward' into an uncaught exception on the IME/typing path. None of the ten call sites (333, 559, 587, 647, 698, 744, 3646, 3701, 3773, 5242) guard against a throw, so this is a contract change (total -> partial) with unupdated callers — in-lane for blast radius and major.
